learning_outcomes.text: Identify and describe basic principles and methods of mechanical engineering.
Understand the principles of composition and classification of composite materials and their mechanical properties.
Understand failure criteria and deterioration mechanisms in composites (delamination, cracking, fatigue).
Explain and interpret theoretical experimental results, technical documentation, phenomena and processes in mechanical engineering.
Know the particularities of polymeric, metallic, and ceramic composite materials used in various industries.
Operate with basic methods and techniques in the field and associate them with specific graphical representations in mechanical engineering.
Ability to perform strength calculations for layered structures and hybrid material elements.
Ability to design optimized composite material structures for strength and reduced weight.
Develop professional conduct oriented towards innovation and responsible use of modern materials.
Ability to independently evaluate the performance and limits of composite structures in engineering applications.
Select and analyze specific bibliographic sources in mechanical engineering.
Demonstrate autonomy in learning specific mechanical engineering issues.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and fundamental notions for the study of composite materials.
Main categories of composite materials and their particularities.
Failure criteria and fracture theories for anisotropic structures.
Main manufacturing methods for composite material structures.
Macromechanical aspects of composite structure calculation.
Micromechanical aspects of composite structure calculation.
Calculation examples regarding the tailoring of composite structure properties.
Behavior in aggressive environments and aging of composite materials.
Non-destructive testing and inspection methods for composite materials.
Numerical modeling of composite structures.
Ecological impact and recycling of composite materials.
Basic notions regarding the design of composite material structures.
Modern trends and research directions in the field of composite materials.
Recap and conclusions.
Presentation of laboratory works and occupational safety regulations.
Determination of volume fraction by complete combustion method.
Tensile testing of [0/90] reinforced composite materials - ASTM D3039.
Tensile testing of [±45] reinforced composite materials - ASTM D3518.
Compression testing of composite materials - ASTM D3410.
Pure shear testing of composite materials - ASTM D5379.
Shear testing of composite materials - ASTM D7078.
Rail shear testing of composite materials - ASTM D-4255.
Bending testing of composite materials - ASTM D790 / D7264.
Charpy/Izod impact testing for composite materials - ASTM D256 / D6110.
Determination of water absorption ASTM D570.
Determination of material constants for composite materials.
Testing composite materials by Arcan method.
Recovery of uncompleted laboratory works.
teaching_methods: Interactive lectures with free exposition and explanation of notions, combined with video-projector use.
Classical format laboratory hours using notion explanation on blackboard and illustration with video-projector.
Prelection and explanation for fundamental concepts.
Applied exercises for consolidation and understanding verification.
Case studies and learning to stimulate critical thinking and creativity.
Laboratory activity to observe material behavior and resistance elements, correlating theory with engineering practice.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory activities (Oral responses, Individual project documentation synthesis)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated by combining scores and weights from all activities. Whole grades from 1 to 10 are awarded. A minimum grade of 5 is required for each assessed component (midterm test, final exam, laboratory activities) and for the overall final grade to pass the discipline and earn credits.
